subject.title: fix: prevent cumulative usage from inflating session context

question: Should this member-authored session-accounting fix be refreshed onto current `main` and landed once the exact-head dependency gate and focused persistence regression pass?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes persisted context state used by compaction, and the current branch’s proof predates its latest force-push; a maintainer should confirm the release-ready merge result rather than infer it from the earlier head.

options.title: Refresh and land after exact-head proof
options.body: Rebase onto current `main`, clear the dependency gate, and rerun the focused cached multi-call abort/persistence proof before merging.

options.title: Pause for broader accounting review
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want the related subagent and large-tool-output context-accounting reports resolved under one broader design review.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current `main`, clear the dependency gate, and rerun the focused cached multi-call abort/persistence proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cached-usage work is the closest established ownership trail for the context-snapshot invariant this PR extends.
